mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year indicates inflationary pressure, leading to potential monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve, which in turn may cause negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased production costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand, which can boost economic growth and lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2%, it indicates a potential economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals strong labor market conditions, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real final sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which can boost corporate earnings and lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% signals accommodative monetary policy, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.
